angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 10,828,571 km at 44.66 pc = 3.24 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 61359: distance 44.663 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.008), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 44.663 +/- 0.357 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 22.0049 +/- 0.2333 mas (same row, RUWE 3.09), 94.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 15.565 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 61359: radius 15.565 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 160.862 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.049) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 10,828,571 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5214 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 61359: effective temperature 5214 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 61359: effective temperature 5214 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.85 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 16 published values span log g 1.888 to 2.847, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.5% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
